DensePose charts · v1 vs v2

What the fold looks like

v1 = the official DensePose charts transferred to SMPL-X. v2 = our re-flattening (Tutte/mean-value embedding) of the four parts where v1 is non-injective: both hands and both feet. Everything else is bit-identical between conventions. Chart squares are coloured by template XYZ; red overlay = texels claimed by 2+ non-adjacent triangles (fold), with severity = 3D distance between claimants. Body views split each part along its thickness axis and paint the surface by an (u,v) hue×brightness checker — a fold makes the SAME colours and checker cells appear on BOTH sides of the limb.

WHY IT MATTERS

Consequences

1 · GT labels: on a folded chart two surface points share one (part,u,v) — a regression target that is a coin flip. This capped hand/foot accuracy until the v2 re-flattening (training on v2 = the A/C/D/E runs). 2 · Garment texture atlases (MCLD-style): the appearance texture is built by warping pixels into chart space — under v1, palm and back-of-hand pixels land on the SAME texels and overwrite each other; no correspondence model, however good, can undo that. 3 · COCO eval: annotations are v1-convention, so v2 models are scored through the exact v2→v1 remap (worth 4.7 AP). The head keeps its official chart in v2; its residual red is SMPL-X hidden geometry (eyeballs, mouth interior) — handled separately by the hidden-faces training mask, not by re-flattening.
